'''Diederik Maarten Samsom ''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈdidərɪk ˈmaːrtə(n) ˈsɑmsɔm|-|Diederik Samsom.ogg}}; born 10 July 1971) is a Dutch environmentalist and retired politician who was the leader of the [[Leader of the Labour Party (Netherlands)|Labour Party]] (''Partij van de Arbeid'', PvdA) from 2012 to 2016. He was the first leader in the 70-year history of the PvdA to have been voted out of his position by party members. He later served as head of cabinet for [[First-Vice-President of the European Commission|First Vice-President of the European Commission]] [[Frans Timmermans]] and his successor [[Wopke Hoekstra]].

Elected to the [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|House of Representatives]] between 30 January 2003 and 14 December 2016, he was elected PvdA [[parliamentary leader]] as well as [[party leader]] on 16 March 2012.<ref>{{cite web|last=Spekman|first=Hans|title=Party Chairman|url=http://nu.pvda.nl/berichten/2012/03/Uitslag-ledenraadpleging-politiek-leider-pvda.html|access-date=16 March 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316192932/http://nu.pvda.nl/berichten/2012/03/Uitslag-ledenraadpleging-politiek-leider-pvda.html|archive-date=16 March 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He lost the Labour Party leadership election to [[Lodewijk Asscher]] in December 2016. Before his election to the House of Representatives he was [[CEO]] of a [[Green energy|green energy company]] and a campaigner for [[Greenpeace|Greenpeace Netherlands]].

== Early life and career ==
Diederik Maarten Samsom was born on 10 July 1971 in [[Groningen]] in the [[Netherlands]]. He was raised in [[Leeuwarden]].<ref name="vk"/> His father worked as an [[internist]] and his mother as a [[physiotherapist]].

Between 1983 and 1989, he attended the Stedelijk Gymnasium (Municipal [[Gymnasium (school)|Gymnasium]]) in [[Leeuwarden]]. There he became interested in physics, and later he went on to study [[applied physics]] at [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref name="stentor">{{Cite journal|last=Abswoude|first=Peter van|title=Colloquium cum Diederik Samsom|journal=Stentor: Acta Scholastica Gymnasii Civitatis Leovardiensis|volume=3|pages=23–25|date=February 2003|language=nl}}</ref> Samsom specialised in [[nuclear physics]] and became a level three radiation protection expert. He graduated in May 1997, obtaining a Dutch [[engineer's degree]] ({{langx|nl|ingenieur|links=no}}).<ref name="Ir.">The title "ir." is like the international engineer's degree.</ref> He was also on the board of the [[students' union|national students' union]] [[Students' union#Netherlands|LSVb]] and edited a yearly edition of the ''Poenboek'', a students' guide relating to monetary issues.

Samsom had been involved in environmental issues long before entering politics. Samsom joined environmental organisation [[Greenpeace|Greenpeace Netherlands]] in September 1995 as a volunteer. He led several campaigns and projects until he resigned in December 2001, after the PvdA offered him a career in politics.<ref name="per">{{cite web |url=http://perdefinitie.nl/?do=profile&mid=116 |title=DIEDERIK SAMSOM |year=2007 |publisher=Stichting Per Definitie |access-date=2008-05-16 |language=nl |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090112153700/http://perdefinitie.nl/?do=profile&mid=116 |archive-date=12 January 2009 |df=dmy }}</ref> He also worked as the CEO of Echte Energie (Real Energy), a small [[green energy]] trading company, from August 2002 until January 2003.<ref name="vk"/>

== Political career ==
Samsom became a member of the [[social democratic]] [[Labour party (Netherlands)|Labour party]] while a student in [[Delft]]. He left the party but rejoined in February 2001. He stood as a candidate in the [[2002 Dutch general election]], but was not elected due to the PvdA receiving insufficient votes in the election. The party regained most of its seats in the [[2003 Dutch general election|2003 election]] and this time Samsom had a higher position (nine)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parlement.com/9291000/modules/hjoixmh6|title=PvdA-kandidaten Tweede Kamerverkiezingen 2003|publisher=Parlement.com|access-date=2008-05-15|language=nl|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081006234804/http://www.parlement.com/9291000/modules/hjoixmh6|archive-date=6 October 2008|df=dmy-all}}</ref> on the list of candidates. He was subsequently sworn in as a member of the [[House of Representatives of the Netherlands|House of Representatives]] on 30 January 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parlement.com/cgi-bin/as.cgi/0291000/c/start/file=/9291000/modulesf/gagaj2gp|title=PvdA en Tweede Kamerverkiezingen 2003|publisher=Parlement.com|access-date=2008-05-15|language=nl}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

=== Red Engineer ===
Together with fellow PvdA parliamentarians [[:nl:Staf Depla|Staf Depla]] and [[Jeroen Dijsselbloem]] he traveled around the country campaigning. They operated under the name ''The Red Engineers'' ({{langx|nl|De rode ingenieurs}}), referring to both their scientific backgrounds and their red overalls. [[NRC Handelsblad|NRC newspaper]] editor Coen van Zwol called their campaign ''fresh, clear and sharp'' (Dutch: fris, helder en scherp).<ref name="Zwol">{{cite news|url=http://www.nrc.nl/achtergrond/article1061536.ece/Diederik_Samsom,_een_ambitieuze_ex-radicaal|title=Diederik Samsom, een ambitieuze ex-radicaal|newspaper=[[NRC Handelsblad]]|date=2008-04-22|first=Coen van|last=Zwol|access-date=2008-05-15|language=nl}}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

=== Parliamentarian ===
[[File:Diederik Samsom.jpg|thumb|upright|Diederik Samsom in 2006]]

Before being admitted as the leader of the Labour party, Samsom was the party's spokesperson on environmental issues: [[sustainability]], [[climate and energy]], [[traffic congestion]] and railway issues and projects. He was nineteenth on the list of candidates in the [[2006 Dutch general election]]s receiving a relative high number of 6248 preferential votes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kiesraad.nl/tweede/virtuele_map/uitslag-van-de |publisher=Kiesraad |title=Uitslag van de Tweede Kamerverkiezing van 22 november 2006 |language=nl |access-date=2008-06-20 |date=2006-11-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512003528/http://www.kiesraad.nl/tweede/virtuele_map/uitslag-van-de |archive-date=12 May 2008 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref>

=== 2008 parliamentary chair election ===
In April 2008, Samsom was a candidate to succeed [[Jacques Tichelaar]] as [[Parliamentary leader|parliament party leader]], but eventually he lost the vote to [[Mariëtte Hamer]].

Jacques Tichelaar became the leader of the parliamentary party shortly after the [[2006 Dutch general election|2006 general election]] in February 2007<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nu.nl/news/976826/11/rss/Jacques_Tichelaar_fractievoorzitter_PvdA.html|title=Jacques Tichelaar fractievoorzitter PvdA|publisher=[[NU.nl]]|date=2007-02-14|access-date=2008-05-18|language=nl}}</ref>  but fell ill in January 2008. He underwent a [[Coronary artery bypass surgery|septuple bypass surgery]] and this took him three months to recuperate. On 16 April, he announced he had decided to resign from office for health reasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ad.nl/binnenland/2227232/PvdAfractieleider_Tichelaar_treedt_af.html|title=PvdA-fractieleider Tichelaar treedt af|newspaper=[[Algemeen Dagblad]]|date=2008-04-16|access-date=2008-05-18|language=nl}}</ref> Tichelaar planned to return as a parliamentarian on 1 July 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nrc.nl/binnenland/article1054353.ece|newspaper=[[NRC Handelsblad]]|title=Fractievoorzitter PvdA legt functie neer|date=2008-04-16|access-date=2008-05-18|language=nl}}{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> As vice parliamentary leader Hamer had led the party in Tichelaar's absence. The next day she decided to run for office.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.depers.nl/binnenland/193419/Hamer-wil-fractieleider-PvdA-worden.html |title=Hamer wil fractieleider PvdA worden |publisher=[[De Pers]] |date=2008-04-17 |access-date=2008-05-18 |language=nl |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719072359/http://www.depers.nl/binnenland/193419/Hamer-wil-fractieleider-PvdA-worden.html |archive-date=19 July 2011 |df=dmy }}</ref> Three days later, Samsom officially announced that he would also compete in the race. Other names were mentioned, but only Samsom and Hamer decided to vie for the position.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nrc.nl/binnenland/article1059492.ece/Samsom_kandidaat_fractievoorzitterschap_PvdA|newspaper=[[NRC Handelsblad]]|title=Samsom kandidaat fractievoorzitterschap PvdA|date=2008-04-21|access-date=2008-05-18|language=nl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080425051223/http://www.nrc.nl/binnenland/article1059492.ece/Samsom_kandidaat_fractievoorzitterschap_PvdA|archive-date=25 April 2008|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> All 33 PvdA parliamentarians gathered two days later to discuss the position and cast their votes, resulting in a victory for Hamer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pvda.nl/renderer.do/menuId/200006406/clearState/true/sf/200006406/returnPage/200006406/itemId/220283403/realItemId/220283403/pageId/200006510/instanceId/37907/nwsbrf/true/nwsbrfd/2008_04_24/|publisher=[[Partij van de Arbeid]]|title=Hamer nieuwe fractievoorzitter|date=2008-04-22|access-date=2008-05-18|language=nl}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>

According to pollster [[Maurice de Hond]], a majority of the 2006 Labour voters preferred Samsom as party leader. Out of a total of 1,500 Labour voters, 26%  favoured Hamer while 42% liked Samsom better. In this poll, of the people who indicated that they would vote for the PvdA in the future, a small majority of 40 to 35 preferred Samsom.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elsevier.nl/nieuws/politiek/artikel.asp?artnr=203154|title=PvdA-kiezer wil Samsom, en niet Hamer|publisher=[[Elsevier (magazine)|Elsevier]]|first=Robin van der|last=Kloor|date=2008-04-24|access-date=2008-05-18|language=nl}}</ref>

===Party leadership===
[[File:Congres maart 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Samsom after his [[victory]] in the leadership election]]

On 22 February 2012, following [[Job Cohen]]'s resignation as party leader, Samsom stood as candidate in the party's leadership ballot which was held among the party members. On 16 March 2012, he obtained a landslide victory with 54% of the vote, with the runner-up [[Ronald Plasterk]] receiving 32% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pvda.nl/berichten/2012/03/Uitslag-ledenraadpleging-politiek-leider-pvda|title=Diederik Samsom politiek leider|language=nl|access-date=17 July 2012|date=16 March 2012|first=Hans|last=Spekman|author-link=Hans Spekman|publisher=[[Labour Party (Netherlands)|PvdA]]|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233155/http://www.pvda.nl/berichten/2012/03/Uitslag-ledenraadpleging-politiek-leider-pvda|url-status=dead}}</ref> Samsom stated he would like to become [[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|prime minister]] should the PvdA become the largest party, or otherwise continue his role of [[Parliamentary group leader|chairman]] of his party in the [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer)]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.trouw.nl/tr/nl/4500/Politiek/article/detail/3226301/2012/03/17/De-energievoorraad-van-Diederik-Samsom-raakt-nooit-op.dhtml |language=nl |title=De energievoorraad van Diederik Samsom raakt nooit op |date=17 March 2012 |access-date=17 July 2012 |newspaper=[[Trouw]]}}</ref>

==== Rutte II: coalition government ====
In the 2012 general election the PvdA, under Samsom's leadership, gained 8 seats and totaled at 38 seats in the Tweede Kamer. After a swift negotiations the PvdA, as second largest party, entered into a coalition with the largest party the VVD. Samsom remained chairman of the PvdA in the Tweede Kamer and [[Lodewijk Asscher]] became vicepremier and minister for Social Affairs and Employment on behalf of the PvdA.

==== EU-Turkey refugee deal ====
During the Dutch Presidency of the Council of the European Union in early 2016, Diederik Samsom is credited with masterminding a key provision in the deal between the EU and Turkey.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2016/03/29/migrantencrisis-samsom-bedacht-de-formule-achter-1604143-a910497|title=Samsom bedacht de formule achter Turkijedeal|website=NRC|date=29 March 2016 |language=nl|access-date=2019-09-13}}</ref> The deal aimed to mitigate the mounting humanitarian crisis in the refugee camps on the Greek islands. Under the provision, for every Syrian refugee being returned to Turkey from the Greek islands, another Syrian would be resettled from Turkey to the EU.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2016/03/18/eu-turkey-statement/|title=EU-Turkey statement, 18 March 2016 - Consilium|website=www.consilium.europa.eu|access-date=2019-09-13}}</ref>

==== 2017 elections: resignation ====
Polls suggest that the Labour party lost most of its electoral base while Samsom was in charge. On 9 December 2016 Samsom lost the [[Leader of the Labour Party (Netherlands)|leadership of the Labour Party]] in an election against [[Lodewijk Asscher]]. He obtained 45,5% of the vote.<ref>{{cite news|author=Joost de Vries |url=http://www.volkskrant.nl/binnenland/asscher-verslaat-samsom-in-lijsttrekkersstrijd-pvda~a4431270/ |title=Asscher verslaat Samsom in lijsttrekkersstrijd PvdA |language=nl |newspaper=[[de Volkskrant]] |date=9 December 2016 |access-date=26 December 2016}}</ref> Samsom resigned from the House of Representatives on 14 December, and was replaced by [[Rien van der Velde]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parlement.com/id/vg9fgopug9zh/d_m_diederik_samsom |title=Ir. D.M. (Diederik) Samsom |language=nl |publisher=Parlement.com |access-date=26 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parlement.com/id/vka0jqjgytue/nieuws/nieuw_tweede_kamerlid_voor_de_pvda_emre |title=Nieuw Tweede Kamerlid voor de PvdA: Emre Ünver |language=nl |publisher=Parlement.com |date=15 December 2016 |access-date=26 December 2016}}</ref> [[Attje Kuiken]] took over the role of group leader of the Labour Party in the House of Representatives on 12 December.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parlement.com/id/vk9ym4f111z3/nieuws/attje_kuiken_nieuwe_fractievoorzitter |title=Attje Kuiken nieuwe fractievoorzitter PvdA |language=nl |publisher=Parlement.com |date=12 December 2016 |access-date=16 December 2016}}</ref>

=== European Commission and years after ===
In November 2019, Samsom became head of cabinet for [[Frans Timmermans]], [[First-Vice-President of the European Commission|First Vice-President of the European Commission]] and [[European Commissioner for Climate Action|Commissioner for Climate Action]]. [[Wopke Hoekstra]] succeeded Timmermans in the latter role in late 2023, while Samsom stayed on. Samsom stepped down in February 2024 as head of cabinet and was succeeded by [[Esther de Lange]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 January 2024 |title=CDA'er Esther de Lange nieuwe kabinetschef Wopke Hoekstra, volgt Diederik Samsom op |trans-title=CDA member Esther de Lange new head of cabinet Wopke Hoekstra, succeeds Diederik Samsom |url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/politiek/cda-er-esther-de-lange-nieuwe-kabinetschef-wopke-hoekstra-volgt-diederik-samsom-op~bb4734ab/ |access-date=31 January 2024 |website=[[de Volkskrant]] |language=nl}}</ref> He became chair of the [[supervisory board]] of state-owned natural gas infrastructure and transportation company [[Gasunie]] in July 2024, saying that he wanted to help execute the [[renewable energy transition]]. He failed to inform the [[European Commission]] of his new position as is required to prevent [[conflicts of interest]], but the body finally allowed the appointment of Samsom under certain conditions.<ref name="vk">{{Cite interview |last=Samsom |first=Diederik |interviewer=Orla McDonald and Eva Rooijers |title=Diederik Samsom: 'Als Nederland niet investeert in groene technologie, is er straks geen industrie meer' |url=https://fd.nl/politiek/1543158/diederik-samsom-als-nederland-niet-investeert-in-groene-technologie-is-er-straks-geen-industrie-meer |access-date=26 January 2025 |website=[[Het Financieele Dagblad]] |date=23 January 2025 |language=nl |url-access=subscription |trans-title=Diederik Samsom: 'If the Netherlands will not invest in green technology, there will not be an industrial sector'}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ballegeer |first=Daan |date=9 August 2024 |title=Diederik Samsom mag van Brussel voor Gasunie werken, onder voorwaarden |trans-title=Brussels allows Samsom to work for Gasunie, under conditions |url=https://fd.nl/politiek/1527105/diederik-samsom-mag-van-brussel-voor-gasunie-werken-onder-voorwaarden |url-access=subscription |access-date=10 August 2024 |website=[[Het Financieele Dagblad]] |language=nl}}</ref>

== Media appearances ==
[[NRC Handelsblad|NRC newspaper]] referred to Samsom as ''quizking'' after he won his fifth televised game show.<ref name="geschiedenis"/> Particularly notable are his consecutive victories in the [[Test the Nation|2005 and 2006 National IQ Tests]].<ref name="Zwol"/> According to the test, he has an IQ of 136.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.trouw.nl/laatstenieuws/laatstenieuws/article899834.ece/Diederik_Samsom_wint_Nationale_IQ_Test|title= Diederik Samsom wint Nationale IQ Test|newspaper=[[Trouw]]|access-date=2008-05-16|language=nl|date=2008-01-23}}</ref> He also won the popular ''[[:nl:Nationale Nieuwsquiz|National News Quiz]]'' in 2005 and 2006<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.volkskrant.nl/binnenland/article534142.ece/Samsom_Jan_Smit_past_beste_bij_PvdA|title=Samsom: Jan Smit past beste bij PvdA|date=2008-05-06|access-date=2008-05-16|language=nl|publisher=[[De Volkskrant]]}}</ref> and in May 2008 he was crowned winner of the ''Big History Quiz''.<ref name="geschiedenis">{{cite news|url=http://www.nrc.nl/media/article1073207.ece/Diederik_Samsom_winnaar_Grote_Geschiedenis_Quiz|title=Diederik Samsom winnaar Grote Geschiedenis Quiz|newspaper=[[NRC Handelsblad]]|date=2008-05-01|access-date=2008-05-16|language=nl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080503004013/http://www.nrc.nl/media/article1073207.ece/Diederik_Samsom_winnaar_Grote_Geschiedenis_Quiz|archive-date=3 May 2008|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Samsom was raised in a [[irreligion|non-religious]] family and considers himself an [[atheism|atheist]]. He is a [[non smoker]] and observes a [[vegetarianism|vegetarian]] diet.<ref name="per"/>{{dead link|date=September 2016}} Samsom divorced in 2016  and has two children. Samsom mentioned them in several political debates and interviews in a for the Netherlands unprecedented and criticized way, including drawing attention to his daughter's disability.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metronieuws.nl/nieuws/dochter-samsom-verdient-bescherming/SrZlgs!prGrtGSWwcr5o/|title=Dochter Samsom verdient bescherming|publisher=[[Metro (Dutch newspaper)|Metro]]|access-date=2012-09-18|language=nl|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104171335/http://www.metronieuws.nl/nieuws/dochter-samsom-verdient-bescherming/SrZlgs!prGrtGSWwcr5o/|archive-date=4 November 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He also involved his private life and family in his 2012 [[Political campaign|electoral campaign]], most notably by featuring his two children in an official party [[Television advertisement|TV advertisement]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/dutch-labor-party-surges-in-opinion-polls-threatens-to-unseat-prime-minister-mark-rutte/2012/09/08/b5097fc6-f98c-11e1-a0a1-b07778c66e04_story.html|title=Dutch Labor party surges in opinion polls, threatens to unseat Prime Minister Mark Rutte|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=2012-09-08|access-date=2012-09-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215222343/https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/dutch-labor-party-surges-in-opinion-polls-threatens-to-unseat-prime-minister-mark-rutte/2012/09/08/b5097fc6-f98c-11e1-a0a1-b07778c66e04_story.html|archive-date=15 December 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.zijonline.nl/2012/06/30/pvda-voorman-diederik-samsom-gebruikt-gehandicapte-dochter-in-campagnespotje/ |title=PvdA-voorman Diederik Samsom gebruikt gehandicapte dochter in campagnespotjfe om stemmen te trekken |publisher=zijonline.nl |date=2012-06-30 |access-date=2012-09-08 |language=nl |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120704130915/http://www.zijonline.nl/2012/06/30/pvda-voorman-diederik-samsom-gebruikt-gehandicapte-dochter-in-campagnespotje/ |archive-date=4 July 2012 |df=dmy }}</ref>

Samsom lived on a [[houseboat]] in [[Broek in Waterland]] with his ex-wife (then girlfriend) and daughter before moving to [[Leiden]], where he still resides as of 2012.<ref name="stentor"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://kiesraad.nl/sites/default/files/BIJLAGE%20bij%20nieuwsbericht%20uitslag%20TK2012.pdf#page=6 |title=Bijlage bij nieuwsbericht - uitslag Tweede Kamerverkiezing 2012 |publisher=Kiesraad |access-date=2012-09-17 |language=nl |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021011107/http://www.kiesraad.nl/sites/default/files/BIJLAGE%20bij%20nieuwsbericht%20uitslag%20TK2012.pdf#page=6 |archive-date=21 October 2012 |df=dmy }}</ref> In a 2012 interview with Marie Claire, Samsom admitted that before his marriage he had been unfaithful "''perhaps once or twice''".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10000872396390443589304577633650987624414|title=U.S.-Styled Campaign Catapults Dutch Labor Leader|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal|date=2012-09-05|access-date=2012-09-16}}</ref>{{Failed verification|This does not appear in the WSJ (it does in the Parool)|date=September 2016}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.parool.nl/parool/nl/3587/POLITIEK-BINNENLAND/article/detail/3298828/2012/08/09/Samsom-had-vroeger-krullen-en-meer-onthullingen.dhtml|title=Samsom had vroeger krullen en meer onthullingen|publisher=[[Parool]]|date=2012-08-09|access-date=2012-09-10|language=nl}}</ref>
